Docs/Embodiments

Embodiments

Understand supported end-effectors and the canonical Panda–Sharpa configuration used for the paper results.

A shared task family, several interfaces

DexArena's research code supports a parallel-jaw gripper and the Sharpa, Wuji and XHand dexterous hands. Each embodiment has its own robot description, controller layout and collection/retargeting configuration. The shared task family enables embodiment studies, but interface support alone does not establish comparable scores.

End-effectorUse and scope
Parallel-jaw gripperGripper-based task interfaces for cross-embodiment studies.
Sharpa Hand22 hand joints per side; Panda + Sharpa is the canonical setup for the manuscript's demonstrations and six-method evaluation.
Wuji HandA separate dexterous-hand robot and retargeting profile; read its registered spaces.
XHandAn additional hand interface with its own joint map, limits and runtime profile.

Read the action space for the selected robot

In the canonical Sharpa setup, one arm uses 7 arm joints plus 22 hand joints, for 29 absolute targets. Bimanual tasks concatenate left arm, right arm, left hand and right hand, for 58 targets. The control mode is pd_joint_pos.

Do not reuse the Sharpa width or joint map for another hand. Inspect the registered robot UID, action space, joint names and limits, and verify the recorded dataset metadata. A matching array length does not establish a matching semantic joint order.

Port a policy with an explicit mapping

  1. Confirm which stage environments are implemented for the desired robot and whether their success conditions and geometry match the comparison.
  2. Map the policy's proprioceptive fields to the robot's actual joints and sensors.
  3. Define the output conversion into absolute controller targets, including hand limits and any retargeting.
  4. Collect or validate embodiment-matched demonstrations rather than treating another hand's joint values as equivalent.
  5. Check short rollouts and replay before running a complete study.

In the research checkout, inspect task/config/hand_variants.py and the relevant modules under task/robots/. See Policy integration for the adapter contract.

Report embodiment studies clearly

State the robot/hand, task IDs, controller, action dimensions, camera profile and any task or asset changes. Publish embodiment-specific results separately from the canonical Panda–Sharpa manuscript scores. Avoid implying that every supported hand has a complete six-method benchmark table.

Use Configurations to preserve the common workstation and timing, and the reproduction checklist to document the differences.
